title: Does an Executable Emulator Validator Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated Network Configuration Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that measured the marginal effect of inserting an executable emulator validator with a bounded repair policy into a generate→validate→repair pipeline versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow. Using a deterministic shared-generation paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 tasks per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) we produced one shared initial candidate per task with gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated the identical candidate under both baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (validator ± repair) conditions. The deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, validator_version = 5.0) enforced workflow_policies encoded in structured task payloads and allowed at most one repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline successes = 120/120; guarded successes = 120/120; paired contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode. We expand methodological detail, representative diagnostics from archived validator traces, design trade-offs, and prescriptive recommendations for future confirmatory studies aimed at exercising repair behavior.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) can map operator intent into concrete configuration commands and promise productivity gains for NetOps. However, syntactically plausible command sequences may violate stateful and sequencing invariants (for example, MTU changes requiring an interface down, or make-before-break uplink switchover) and produce semantic failures visible only in closed-loop execution. Prior literature therefore argues for integrating runtime validators, emulators, or deterministic veto layers to detect or prevent unsafe enactment before changes reach production. Measuring the marginal contribution of such validators requires executable tests that capture temporal and group-level invariants rather than token-level correctness alone. We executed a preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) whose narrow confirmatory question is mechanistic: for identical generator outputs, can an executable emulator validator and a bounded repair policy reduce emulator-observed semantic failures relative to an LLM-only suggestion workflow? The shared-initial-candidate paired design isolates validator/repair effects by removing generator-induced variance so that any discordance between conditions is attributable to the guarded subsystem.
sections.related_work: Two research strands motivate our design. First, executable and closed-loop NetOps benchmarks reveal that evaluating only generated text or command syntax underestimates operational risk: emulation and digital-twin tests expose sequencing, reachability, and group-availability errors missed by static checks. Recent executable-benchmark and tool papers provide empirical evidence that closed-loop tests detect these higher-order errors [see NetConfArena; Benchmarking LLM-Driven Network Configuration Repair; Aether]. Second, the tool-augmented agent literature advocates architectures that delegate safety-critical checks to deterministic subsystems (veto layers, canaries, generate→validate→repair) to bound autonomy risk. Surveys and architectural proposals emphasize runtime verification and explainability as deployment enablers. Our study complements these works by focusing on the validator/repair marginal effect under a shared-generation protocol: unlike generator-focused studies that conflate generator variability with verification efficacy, the paired design reported here isolates whether a validator can improve outcomes when generator output is held constant. The experiment therefore informs methodological choices for comparing verification subsystems rather than claiming broad external generality across generator families or production heterogeneity.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. The study was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) prior to execution. The confirmatory design was a paired-binary comparison with N=120 distinct tasks deterministically partitioned into three topology classes (40 per class). The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the prespecified test was the exact two-sided McNemar. A paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was prespecified. The protocol enforced a repair budget of ≤1 repair iteration per guarded episode, deterministic emulator resets between tasks, and explicit exclusion rules for technical/instrumentation failures.

Task generation, structured payload, and validator semantics. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, a natural-language intent, an explicit required_sequence (canonical ordered operations), and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, level). The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) which (a) executed the shared candidate in an emulator of initial_state, (b) enforced workflow_policies encoded in the task payload (examples: must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, make-before-break patterns) as executable checks, and (c) emitted structured validator_traces including validation_before, validation_after, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, violation_codes, observed_touched_field_count, and repair_applied. The preregistered repair policy triggered at most one repair only when validator.violation_count > 0.

Shared-generation paired design and instrumentation. For each task we called the declared model (gpt-5-mini) once to produce a single shared_initial_candidate; that candidate was evaluated in both baseline and guarded conditions. This used model_calls_used = 120 (one shared generation per pair) against a planned maximum_model_calls = 240. The harness enforced deterministic container resets, provider-call auditing (hosted_model_call_event_count = 120; cache_miss_count = 120), and contamination detection (duplicate-output and cross-condition cache-key reuse heuristics) per the preregistration. Deterministic reconciliation confirmed complete_pair_count = 120 and no technical exclusions.

Scoring and analysis. Each paired episode produced a binary semantic outcome scored by the emulator: pass (semantic_success = 1) if the emulator-observed final_state met expected_final_state and required_sequence constraints, fail = 0 otherwise. Confirmatory testing executed the exact two-sided McNemar on the paired binary outcomes; the paired-difference CI used the prespecified paired-bootstrap-percentile procedure (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Sensitivity analyses and secondary endpoints (repair incidence, model-call counts) were prespecified but contingent on observed repair activity.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcome. The run completed without technical exclusions. Condition-level outcomes: baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0. Paired contingency: n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Validator traces report repair_applied = false for every guarded episode; consequently no repair-provider-call artifacts exist.

Per-topology and representative diagnostics. The preregistered deterministic partition produced 40 tasks in each topology class. Per-topology counts: Edge (40) baseline = 40/40, guarded = 40/40; Core (40) baseline = 40/40, guarded = 40/40; Leaf–spine (40) baseline = 40/40, guarded = 40/40. Representative archived validator traces show parsed_command_count matching required_command_count, validation_after.valid = true, observed_touched_field_count consistent with task difficulty metadata (level ∈ {medium, hard, very_hard}), and validator.violation_count = 0. These diagnostics confirm that the harness exercised multiple policy-complexity motifs (shutdown→configure→restore, make-before-break uplink switchover, paired atomic MTU changes) even though generator outputs satisfied the structured constraints under the frozen prompting strategy.

Repair and secondary endpoints. Because validator.violation_count = 0 across the run, no repairs were applied and secondary endpoints quantifying repair incidence are vacuous in this execution. The deterministic_reconciliation and provider-call audits (hosted_model_call_event_count = 120, cache_miss_count = 120) corroborate complete accounting and absence of contamination or technical failures.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of a ceiling outcome. The shared-generation paired design isolates validator/repair marginal effects by holding the generator output constant between conditions. A direct consequence is that if the generator—under the chosen prompt, model, and task bank—produces valid candidates for most or all tasks, the guarded pipeline cannot exercise repair and therefore cannot reduce semantic failures relative to the baseline. The observed degenerate contingency (n_11=120) and the resulting McNemar p = 1.0 with a degenerate bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00] are statistical expressions of this ceiling: under the preregistered resampling scheme, zero discordant pairs produce identical resamples and hence a zero-width percentile CI.

Design trade-offs, pragmatic recommendations, and next steps. The paired shared-generation protocol increases internal validity for isolating validator effects but can under-exercise repair when the generator is well-calibrated for the chosen corpus. To meaningfully exercise repair in future confirmatory studies (while preserving preregistered rigor) we recommend prespecified adjustments guided by the archived difficulty metadata and the observed absence of violations:
- Independent-condition generation arms: allow separate initial generations per condition so guarded pipelines can intercept generator-induced errors produced under prompt or sampling variability; adjust analysis to account for generator variance.
- Controlled prompt perturbations: prespecify perturbation variants or sampling temperatures on a subset of tasks to increase generator error incidence while retaining paired blocks for internal control.
- Task stratification toward high-complexity strata: allocate more pairs to 'very_hard' difficulty and higher dependency_rule_count to raise the prior probability of generator-caused violations.
- Exploratory repair-budget arms: allow >1 repair iteration in exploratory arms to observe repair convergence dynamics and resource costs.

Operational implications and auditability. Even when unused, a deterministic validator that emits structured traces (validation_before/after, touched fields, violation codes, repair_applied flags) supports operator auditability, post-hoc diagnosis, and compliance reporting. Instrumented accounting (provider-call audits, deterministic reconciliation) supplies reproducible artifacts for retrospective failure analysis and governance reviews. The experiment highlights that empirical claims about repair benefits require careful experimental framing: if generators rarely produce invalid candidates under a frozen prompt, the guard will be idle by design.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is strong here (deterministic provisioning, exhaustive provider-call audits, zero exclusions). Construct validity is limited by the synthetic task payloads and by the validator's finite encoding of workflow policies; some vendor-specific or partial-observability failure modes are not represented. External validity is constrained by the single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), a frozen prompting strategy, and a synthetic deterministic corpus. Conclusion validity is affected by the statistical ceiling: the preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure ≈ 0.40 targeting an absolute reduction of 0.15; observed baseline = 0.00 violates those assumptions and renders the confirmatory McNemar test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness with a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini). All 120 shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator, yielding n_11 = 120 and a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The run documents a ceiling for this curated synthetic task bank and demonstrates that a shared-generation paired design can mask repair benefits that would appear if generators sometimes produced invalid candidates. Our principal scientific contribution is methodological: we show how a preregistered, artifact-rich paired design cleanly isolates validator/repair marginal effects and how deterministic archival artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, provider-call audits, and reconciliation files) enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing even when the primary confirmatory test is degenerate. Archived artifacts support follow-up studies that relax the shared-generation constraint, compare generator families, expand repair budgets, and evaluate more production-rooted corpora to quantify repair utility under realistic generator variance.

No contamination flags or technical exclusions occurred. Representative archival artifacts (task manifests, responses, validator traces, condition summaries, paired contingency table, and deterministic reconciliation) were archived at the time of execution for independent verification. No manual post-lock edits of technical manuscript content were performed.
limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
